newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB shares slip on "unbundling" report.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB shares slip on "unbundling" report.

text.p: Shares in pay television company British Sky Broadcasting Plc extended recent heavy falls on Monday as a newspaper report highlighted a potential threat to revenues.
A report in the Guardian newsapaper said television watchdog the ITC could move to outlaw the system of selling "bundles" of basic and premium subscription channels.
The report helped push BSkyB shares 11.5p lower to 442p by 1125 GMT, just above 12-month lows.

BSkyB shares have crashed more than 25 percent over the past fortnight amid concern over the loss of key executives and the forced sale of an equity stake in a UK digital terrestrial television venture.
An ITC spokesman confirmed the watchdog was reviewing the system of selling channels in bundles and that it expected to report its conclusions by the end of July.
There was no immediate comment from BSkyB.
Analysts said the hint of further bad news was enough to depress BSkyB shares, given their current weakness.
